<div class="slick-on-page cls-inserted" style="min-height: 200px;"></div><h2><strong>Mongolian Beef Recipe </strong></h2>
<p>If you asked me what I like about this Mongolian beef recipe, I would have a hard time deciding. First of all, it’s Chinese food—I mean who doesn’t like Chinese?</p>
<p>Secondly, the meat is super tender, then there’s the sauce that goes with this Mongolian beef recipe. It is sweet from the brown sugar, with hints of ginger and garlic, then rounded off with soy sauce. This Mongolian beef sauce is like a warm hug on a chilly evening—it’s that good!</p>
<h3><strong>The Best Meat for this Mongolian Beef Recipe</strong></h3>
<p>Flank steak is the typical choice of meat for stir-fried Asian-inspired recipes like this one. But, anything from New York strip steak, to even beef chuck can be used with good results.</p><div class="slick-inline-search-panel cls-inserted" data-config="in-content-DCM" style="min-height: 350px; margin: 50px 15px;"></div>
<h2><strong>Tips for Success for this Easy Mongolian Beef Recipe:</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Keep it tender</strong> – cut the meat into thin strips, against the grain, to keep the beef tender.</li>
<li><strong>Make slices even</strong> – cutting the meat into as even slices is the best way to get an even cook. About 1/4 inch wide is a perfect size.</li>
<li><strong>Do not overcook</strong> – make this easy Mongolian beef recipe even faster by quickly searing the meat in batches will give you crispy, but tender beef.</li>
<li><strong>Control the heat</strong> – add as much or as little of Sriracha sauce to make it desired spiciness.</li>
<li><strong>Use fresh garlic</strong> – don’t substitute for dry or pre-peeled garlic, to keep the flavor extra fresh.</li>
</ul>

<h2>How to Make Mongolian Beef</h2>
<ol>
<li>Pat dry the beef, then cut against the grain into thin strips.</li>
<li>Add to a ziplock bag together with the cornstarch and shake to coat evenly.</li>
<li>Preheat a heavy-bottomed skillet with oil, then sear the pepper quickly, remove to a plate.</li>
<li>In the same manner, quickly saute the onion, remove to a plate.</li>
<li>In batches, quickly sear pieces of beef, remove to a plate.</li>
<li>Add all ingredients for the sauce into the skillet and cook until slightly thickened.</li>
<li>Add beef, onion, pepper and toss to coat, then cook to heat through.</li>
<li>Lastly, add the chopped scallions and toss to combine.</li>
<li>Serve with hot rice.</li>
</ol>

		<h3 class="wprm-recipe-header">Instructions</h3>
				<div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-group">
						<h4 class="wprm-recipe-group-name wprm-recipe-instruction-group-name">How to make Mongolian Beef</h4>
						<ol class="wprm-recipe-instructions">
								<li class="wprm-recipe-instruction">
										<div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><p>In a ziplock bag combine the <span class="wprm-dynamic-quantity">1/2 cup cornstarch and 2 lb of cut into strips</span>, close it and shake for the beef strips to be fully and evenly coated in cornstarch. </p></div>
														</li>
								<li class="wprm-recipe-instruction">
										<div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><p>Preheat a large skillet over high heat, then add enough oil to coat the bottom of the skillet. Next, add <span class="wprm-dynamic-quantity">3 </span>cut up bell peppers and quickly cook them for about 3-4 minutes, stirring often. As soon as the bell peppers are browned slightly, remove them to a separate bowl. Do not overcook them, they should still have a bit of a bite to them. <wprm-code><br><br></wprm-code></p><p>Lastly, tilt the skillet to the side and remove the bell peppers to a separate bowl, leaving the oil behind.</p></div>
														</li>
								<li class="wprm-recipe-instruction">
										<div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><p>Add the onions to the skillet and sear for about 3-4 minutes, just trying to char up the sides.  Add more oil if needed. Tilt the skillet and remove the onion to the bowl with peppers, leaving the oil behind. </p></div>
														</li>
								<li class="wprm-recipe-instruction">
										<div id="AdThrive_Recipe_2_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-recipe adthrive-recipe-1 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px;"></div><div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><p>Next, add the rest of the oil and add the beef strips, shaking off the excess of cornstarch and cook in a single layer in batches for about 1 minute per side. Transfer the cooked beef to a separate bowl. Do not overcrowd the pan. Beef needs to be seared, not cooked in its own juices. Keep adding the oil as needed after cooking each batch.</p></div>
														</li>
							</ol>
		</div>
				<div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-group">
						<h4 class="wprm-recipe-group-name wprm-recipe-instruction-group-name">Mongolian Beef Sauce</h4>
						<ol class="wprm-recipe-instructions">
								<li class="wprm-recipe-instruction">
										<div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><p>Drain off the remaining oil from the skillet leaving the stuck on beef bits. </p><p><span class="wprm-dynamic-quantity">Next add 1/2 cup of soy sauce, 1/2 cup water and 1/2 cup brown sugar, 2 tsp of ginger powder and the 4 cloves of minced garlic to the pan and let it come to a boil, scraping off the bits off the bottom of the skillet. </span> </p><p>Boil for about 1-2 minutes to reduce the sauce. Then, add Sriracha sauce if desired.</p></div>
														</li>
							</ol>
		</div>
				<div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-group">
						<h4 class="wprm-recipe-group-name wprm-recipe-instruction-group-name">Bring everything together</h4>
						<ol class="wprm-recipe-instructions">
								<li class="wprm-recipe-instruction">
										<div class="wprm-recipe-instruction-text"><p>Add the beef back into the sauce and stir to coat it in the sauce. Allow to come to a boil, which should thicken the sauce. Next add the bell peppers, cooked onion, and the green onion stalks and stir to heat through. </p></div>
														</li>
							</ol>
		</div>

<p>I made this with a chunk of sirloin tip steak I had in my freezer. I had to be very careful to slice the steak against the grain and had to turn and cut several pieces apart as the grain was going in different directions.   Also, my steak was still a little frozen so that assisted in slicing it thin. That may have been the problem Alina had. But, if she did indeed slice her flank steak against the grain, it should not have been tough regardless of how thick the slices were. Don’t know why that happened. The only change I made to the recipe is that I added some Worcestershire as Bryan Walsh had. Served it over bulgar wheat and it was delicious and will definitely make this again. Great recipe!</p>

<p>This recipe is great.  The meat (I used New York) was so tender.  I will definitely make this again.<br>
I would make the following changes or additions:<br>
1) Add pepper to the corn starch to give the meat a little more seasoning/flavor.<br>
2) The 1/4″ strips of meat I cut were too long.  I would make sure the meat is more bitesize.<br>
3) I chose to make the sauce have a little more body, so I added a corn starch slurry to the sauce as it was being reduced.</p>
